[F3] The compiler enumerates every finite B6 word and dovetails all
precision levels; an accepted certificate implies both operator errors are
strictly below $\varepsilon$.
[[alg-qa-37-exhaustive-b6-block-pair-compiler]]

[F4] For a $d\times d$ matrix, $\|A\|_F\le\sqrt d\|A\|_{\rm op}$, and $\|A\|_{\rm op}\le\|A\|_F$.
[[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]]

[A1] Assume exactly $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as used by [F1].
[[def-countable-choice]]

## Proof

1.1 The product of open operator-norm $\varepsilon/128$-balls around $T_5,T_8$ is a neighborhood in $SU(5)\times SU(8)$. By [A1] and [F1], it meets the normalized B6 image, so there is one finite braid word $b_*$ with both block operator errors less than $\varepsilon/128$. For dimension $d\le8$, the real-coordinate $\ell^1$ norm of a complex matrix is at most $\sqrt2 d\|A\|_F\le\sqrt2 d^{3/2}\|A\|_{\rm op}\le32\|A\|_{\rm op}$ by [F4]. Hence the exact coordinate-sum distance in either block is strictly less than $\varepsilon/4$. [A1, F1, F4, given, choose, algebra]

2.1 Fix this finite word. Its exact block matrices and the targets have coordinate approximants converging to their entries by [F2]–[F3]. Therefore $s_{d,b_*,p}$ converges to the real-coordinate $\ell^1$ distance between the exact word block and target; by step 1.1 that limit is less than $\varepsilon/4$. Since $4d2^{-p}\to0$, some finite $p$ makes both certificates strictly below $\varepsilon$. Dovetailing eventually examines $(b_*,p)$, and certificate soundness [F3] ensures acceptance. Thus the procedure halts. ACω enters only through [A1] and [F1]; density gives no search-index bound. [F2, F3, A1, step 1.1, algebra, F1] ∎

[F3] The compiler enumerates every finite B6 word and dovetails all precision levels. Its rational interval procedure and target-name requests supply the stated coordinate approximants, and it returns exactly when both displayed rational tests pass. [[alg-qa-37-exhaustive-b6-block-pair-compiler]]

[F4] For a $d\times d$ matrix, $\|A\|_F\le\sqrt d\|A\|_{\rm op}$, and $\|A\|_{\rm op}\le\|A\|_F$.
[[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]]

[A1] Assume exactly $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as used by [F1].
[[def-countable-choice]]

## Proof

1.1 Fix any word and precision inspected by [F3]. For a $d\times d$ complex matrix whose real and imaginary entry coordinates have errors at most $2^{-p}$, summing their squares bounds the Frobenius error by $d\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$. The word and target approximants from [F2]--[F3] thus have two errors totaling at most $2d\sqrt2\,2^{-p}<3d\,2^{-p}$. The triangle inequality gives $\|B_d(b)-T_d\|_F\le\|P_{d,b,p}-Q_{d,p}\|_F+3d2^{-p}$. [F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

1.2 The rational sum $s_{d,b,p}$ of absolute real and imaginary coordinates dominates $\|P_{d,b,p}-Q_{d,p}\|_F$. Hence [F4] gives $\|B_d(b)-T_d\|_{\rm op}\le s_{d,b,p}+3d2^{-p}<s_{d,b,p}+4d2^{-p}$. If the corresponding rational test passes, this is strictly below $\varepsilon$. Both passing tests therefore certify the two strict block-error bounds without any choice assumption; [A1] is used only for termination below. [F4, step 1.1, given, algebra]

2.1 The product of open operator-norm $\varepsilon/128$-balls around $T_5,T_8$ is a neighborhood in $SU(5)\times SU(8)$. By [A1] and [F1], it meets the normalized B6 image, so there is one finite braid word $b_*$ with both block operator errors less than $\varepsilon/128$. For dimension $d\le8$, the real-coordinate $\ell^1$ norm of a complex matrix is at most $\sqrt2 d\|A\|_F\le\sqrt2 d^{3/2}\|A\|_{\rm op}\le32\|A\|_{\rm op}$ by [F4]. Hence the exact coordinate-sum distance in either block is strictly less than $\varepsilon/4$. [A1, F1, F4, given, choose, algebra]

3.1 Fix this finite word. Its exact block matrices and the targets have coordinate approximants converging to their entries by [F2]–[F3]. Therefore $s_{d,b_*,p}$ converges to the real-coordinate $\ell^1$ distance between the exact word block and target; by step 2.1 that limit is less than $\varepsilon/4$. Since $4d2^{-p}\to0$, some finite $p$ makes both certificates strictly below $\varepsilon$. Dovetailing eventually examines $(b_*,p)$, and the return rule [F3] triggers acceptance. Step 1.2 supplies both strict block-error bounds for the returned word. Thus the procedure halts. ACω enters only through [A1] and [F1]; density gives no search-index bound. [F2, F3, A1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra, F1] ∎
